_doc: Per-uid audit of ALL 196 Mercedes sheets in car-meshes/audit/mercedes/, 2026-08-11. Mercedes was swept and published BEFORE the glazing ruling (2026-08-09), before the tyre ruling and before glass_probe existed, so its cars were cleared against a standard that could not see two whole classes of defect. This closes that gap. CORRECTION to the brief: 80 of the 196 were NOT unaudited -- they are the 'clean' triage bucket audited on 2026-08-08 and recorded in the `verdicts` block of this file's previous version, which is preserved below as `_superseded_2026_08_08`. 116 had never been audited. Every one of the 196 has now been re-judged against the current rulings. TWO INDEPENDENT WITNESSES, neither allowed to overrule the other on ground it cannot see: (1) the glTF via glass_probe -- decisive for glazing and for the flat/global-alpha shells, all of which the sheet is structurally blind to; (2) the eye on the four-view sheet -- decisive for pose, exploded kits, scans, scope and proportions, none of which the glTF sees. `sheet_admissible_for_glazing` records whether ANY material name matches the render worker's override list (glass|window|windscreen|windshield|screen|vidro|glas|scheibe|fenster); where it is true the worker did NOT force transmission=1.0 and the sheet is an honest witness for glazing, where false the sheet's clear glass is manufactured and worthless.
_glazing_is_the_headline: 77 of 196 have opaque glazing, 57 of them PROVEN from a glazing-named material that is alphaMode=OPAQUE at alpha 1.0. 64 of the 66 hard material fails carry a glazing name that matches the worker's override list, which means their sheets render PERFECT CLEAR GLASS and always did. The Mercedes-Benz CLE-450 (#138) is the cleanest illustration: a beautiful sheet with deep-tinted glass and a visible interior, and a glTF in which Windshield1Mtl, Hdcledoorglassltint1Mtl and Hdcledoorglassl1Mtl are all alpha 1.0 OPAQUE. Eight cars the 2026-08-08 audit PASSED are now hard material fails on this evidence.
_alpha_shells_are_one_family: 8 global-alpha shells, and they are not independent finds -- every one carries the identical signature: EVERY material alphaMode=BLEND at alpha 0.25, carpaint and tire included, with '.NNN' material suffixes running 200-256 (carpaint.201/tire.201, carpaint.254/tire.253 ...). That is the same fingerprint CLAUDE.md records for the Volvo XC60 and the two Mazdas, so this is one upstream scene split into many cars, not a Mercedes problem. The G500 #163 is the warning: its sheet looks solid and premium because a 25%-opaque white body over a white studio floor reads as white, and the glass-named materials got the worker's alpha=1.0 override on top. Only the glTF sees it.
_tyres_could_not_be_decided_here: NO car in this wave was passed or failed on tyre colour, and that is deliberate. A glTF tyre probe was written for this audit (pipeline/ingest/tyre_probe.py) and validated against retro_tyre_audit.json's 131 live cars: RECALL 0 of 8 on ground-truth tyre-fails, with 13 false alarms on 108 ground-truth-ok cars. Five of the eight real failures carry a genuinely DARK tyre material (tire at 0.106, rubber at 0.012, tire at 0.008). The defect is a per-corner RENDER artefact in the wheel meshes and the rig; no reading of the material table can see it, and the sheet is a candidate finder only. Tyres on this marque need a RED control render, which is GPU work this audit did not have.
_pose_is_fail_rerender_not_a_scrap: 4 cars (#84 M-class, #93 and #94 A-Class W169, #113 ML W163) render upside down or on their side in all four tiles. Per CLAUDE.md this is the render-side inversion at handler.py:1007 -- an argmin tie under ~1% between two near-equal extents. It is DETERMINISTIC per asset, so re-rendering the same file cannot fix it and the GLB itself is likely fine. Marked fail-rerender, never scrapped.
_duplicates: The GLS 580 is a re-upload swarm: SEVEN uploads at exactly 361,236 faces from seven different uploaders, plus two more at 362,630 and one at 361,616 -- about ten copies of one mesh. The G63 W464 appears four times at exactly 230,325. dupe_check's near-proximity rule is a CANDIDATE finder only and was not allowed to group anything: on this marque it again produced obvious false positives (the W124 saloon vs the C124 coupe 760 apart are different body styles; the G63 vs the GLA35 2,316 apart are different cars). It also has a RECALL gap -- see MERCEDES_DUPES.json's note on the #88/#116 pair, 2 faces apart and vetoed by a title-overlap test it should not have needed.
_what_i_got_wrong_mid_audit: I built tyre_probe expecting it to settle the tyre question cheaply and recorded a first pass in which 16 ground-truth-OK cars scored 'pale'. Two bugs in it were MANUFACTURING failures: textures behind KHR_texture_basisu/EXT_texture_webp raised KeyError so the texture was never read, and an unread texture scored as opaque white even though the factor on a textured material is a multiplier and is [1,1,1] on nearly all of them. Both are fixed. The recall was still 0/8 afterwards, so the tool was demoted to an evidence recorder rather than shipped as a gate. Separately I first read the G500 #163 sheet as a clean pass; the glTF showed it is a global-alpha shell.

_superseded_2026_08_08._coverage_finding: TESTED AND CONFIRMED: all 5 entries in the Mercedes clean set with body-material coverage under 0.10 failed to recolour -- every one rendered its own colour under --colour silver (red, white, black, white, white). Coverage under ~10% means the classifier latched onto trim or a badge, not the body paint. 'clean' only requires mats>=1, so these passed triage. Low cov is a PREDICTOR of recolour failure (the GL350 at cov=0.114 also renders white, so the band is a gradient, not a cliff at 0.10) and should gate the colour bake, not just the eye. 5/5 in this set; consistent with Toyota #41 (pink) and #62 (black), which were also split/low-coverage.

They are completely different vehicles -- a coachbuilt stretch and a 1970s coupe -- so face proximity alone is not identity. The rule flags CANDIDATES for the eye; it must never auto-group. Two of four flagged pairs were real duplicates (GL350, SLS Electric), this one is a false positive, and the C124/W124 pair remains to check.

_superseded_2026_08_08._wheel_void_correction: Two passes CORRECTED to fail after the owner challenged them. The signature is per-SIDE: left wheels render as black voids, right wheels show full spokes. Three diagnoses were tried and only the third held: (1) 'it is lighting' -- wrong, lighting darkens a surface, it does not delete it; (2) 'flipped normals, set doubleSided' -- wrong, all 36 materials were already doubleSided; (3) 'near-black metal mirror' -- rim_dark IS baseColor 0.018 with glTF's default metallicFactor=1.0, but lifting it fixed only the RIGHT wheels. The left wheels are a mirrored duplicate with inverted geometry and need mesh surgery. WHAT SETTLED IT: applying the change and re-rendering. Do not judge a wheel fault from a static sheet alone -- if some views show spokes and others do not, check whether the split is by SIDE before calling it lighting.
